stem: A GP can see an ear canal foreign body but is unsure whether office removal will be straightforward. What is the best next step?

options.text: Refer to ENT if in doubt
Keep repeating blind attempts until it comes out
Send the family home for routine review only
Start oral antibiotics before trying anything else
Use warm oil regardless of the object

explanation: Refer to ENT if in doubt. When ear canal foreign body removal is not clearly straightforward, specialist referral is the safest next step.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because uncertainty about straightforward removal should prompt referral to ENT rather than repeated or improvised attempts.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because repeated blind attempts increase the risk of canal trauma and are not the recommended approach.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because simple observation without a plan is not appropriate when the clinician is unsure about removal.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because oral antibiotics do not address the foreign body and are not the next step in uncomplicated cases.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because warm oil is not a universal treatment for ear foreign bodies and is only considered in specific situations.
